page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance configured with 16 vCPUs and 64 GB of RAM. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture, this server features 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating with dedicated CPU allocation. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports hardware-accelerated instructions such as AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI, though it lacks AVX-512 capabilities. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPU resources.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core testing placing the instance in the top 25% of evaluated systems. Multi-core performance falls into the average range, as demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 21390.8 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9335.0. Memory bandwidth is stable, registering 1013.33 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 93.7 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Cryptographic and database operations also perform within average parameters, with Passmark database operations reaching 6799.65 and Redis SET operations processing at 14.74 million operations per second.

The n2d-standard-16 offers a balanced resource profile, making it a cost-efficient option for workloads requiring steady compute and memory allocation without the premium cost of specialized memory-optimized or compute-optimized hardware. The primary tradeoffs include the complete absence of local NVMe storage and GPU acceleration, which limits its utility for high-speed local caching or deep learning tasks. This instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, software compilation, database operations, and moderate multi-threaded decompression tasks.

The hardware configuration lacks local storage and GPU accelerators but includes 32 MB of L3 cache and supports AES and AVX instruction sets. Benchmarks show strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% on stress-ng, while multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics remain in the average tier. With a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance provides a cost-efficient resource profile for standard enterprise workloads. It is suited for static web serving, software compilation, database operations, and general-purpose application hosting.
